title: The Pinkerton Detective Agency
summary: Hosts Josh and Chuck trace the history of the Pinkerton National Detective Agency, founded by Alan Pinkerton in 1850. Topics include his Scottish Chartist background and emigration to Chicago, his early work as a cooper and deputy sheriff, abolitionist ties and John Brown, the 1861 plot to kill Lincoln in Baltimore and Kate Warren's night watch (origin of the "we never sleep" eye logo), Pinkerton's Civil War intelligence work and inflated Confederate troop estimates, the Rogues Gallery criminal records, the agency's code of conduct, Pinkerton's dime-novel style detective books, Wild West train robberies (Reno Gang), the James Gang and the lantern attack on the James home, the Molly Maguires informant case, anti-union strikebreaking including the 1892 Homestead strike, the Ohio ban, the agency's later history (Securitas acquisition in 1999), and Alan Pinkerton's death in 1884. The episode ends with a listener mail segment about GPS devices used by cyclists.

segments.title: Opening banter and introduction to the Pinkertons
segments.summary: Hosts open with countdown banter and tangents, then introduce the Pinkerton Detective Agency as a legendary private detective firm with a mixed reputation, noting Alan Pinkerton's self-mythologizing.

segments.title: Alan Pinkerton's early life and Chicago career
segments.summary: Pinkerton's birth in Scotland, Chartist involvement, emigration to Dundee, Illinois, work as a cooper, discovery of counterfeiters, deputy sheriff role in Kane County, and move to Cook County.

segments.title: Founding the agency and abolitionist work
segments.summary: The agency is founded in 1850; Pinkerton assists the Underground Railroad and is friends with John Brown, paying for travel of freed enslaved people to Detroit.

segments.title: Early clients and Lincoln connection
segments.summary: The agency's early work for railroads such as the Illinois Central, whose attorney was Lincoln and whose president was McClellan, and Pinkerton's photo with Lincoln at Antietam.

segments.title: Baltimore plot against Lincoln and Kate Warren
segments.summary: Pinkerton uncovers a plot to assassinate Lincoln in Baltimore; Lincoln is disguised and escorted by Kate Warren overnight, giving rise to the 'we never sleep' motto and eye logo.

segments.title: Hiring women detectives
segments.summary: Kate Warren is hired in 1856 and later heads the female detective bureau; the hosts compare this with Lola Baldwin, the first sworn policewoman in the US in 1908.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Ad break.

segments.title: Civil War intelligence work
segments.summary: Pinkerton heads Union secret service under McClellan, uncovers Rose O'Neal Greenhow's spy ring, but overestimates Confederate troop strength, and leaves military intelligence in 1862.

segments.title: Rogues Gallery and criminal records
segments.summary: Pinkerton adopts Bertillon's mugshot and measurement ideas, creating the Rogues Gallery of standardized photos and handwriting samples, a forerunner of criminal databases.

segments.title: Agency code of conduct and detective fiction
segments.summary: The agency's code of conduct (no bribes, no divorce cases, no scandal cases, no reward money) and Pinkerton's true-crime style detective books featuring Kate Warren.

segments.title: Wild West train robberies and the Reno Gang
segments.summary: After the Civil War, the agency hunts train robbers, including the Reno Gang, recovering a large amount of cash and capturing members; one was lynched by locals.

segments.title: James Gang and the lantern attack
segments.summary: The Pinkertons pursue the James Gang; informant Joseph Whicher is murdered, and in 1875 a lantern thrown at the James family home kills Archie and maims Zerelda James, damaging the agency's reputation.

segments.title: Other famous manhunts
segments.summary: Mention of the Butch Cassidy and Sundance Kid chase to Bolivia and the Apple Dumpling Gang executions.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Ad break.

segments.title: Turn to corporate and labor espionage
segments.summary: The agency sides with corporations, infiltrating labor organizations and workplaces to report on union organizing; railway conductors warn members about Pinkerton spies.

segments.title: Molly Maguires case
segments.summary: Pinkerton agent James McParland infiltrates Irish coal miners in Pennsylvania; his testimony leads to executions of twenty men, a process the hosts describe as a private-company-run trial.

segments.title: Homestead strike of 1892
segments.summary: Carnegie Steel and Henry Clay Frick hire about 300 Pinkertons to break the union; a long armed battle with workers leaves about a dozen dead, followed by National Guard deployment. Congress investigates and Ohio bans Pinkertons.

segments.title: Later history, pop culture, and Alan Pinkerton's death
segments.summary: Securitas acquires the agency in 1999; the Pinkerton name persists in security work and films. Alan Pinkerton dies in 1884 from a gangrenous tongue injury; Kate Warren is buried in his family plot.

segments.title: Listener mail: GPS and cycling
segments.summary: Listener Deanna explains why Garmin GPS devices remain popular with cyclists.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts thank the listener and close the show.
